key_insight: Passive syndrome histories can be ambiguous, so safe quantum error-correction updates need extra calibration measurements and drift-aware certification before trusting AI advice.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum hardware, this work provides a practical decision rule to accept only recovery updates that are provably beneficial under uncertainty, reducing the risk of AI-driven harmful control changes.
method: Showed that opposite coherent X rotations can generate identical passive syndrome-history distributions in an odd-distance square toric code.
Used terminal logical measurements on known calibration states to recover the missing sign information needed for safe recovery selection.
Built an evaluator that accepts an update only when calibration confidence and a justified drift bound certify improvement over the current recovery.
evidence_signal: Simulations of advice attacks and noisy surface-code experiments showed that the certification checks rejected harmful proposals while retaining beneficial updates, with a validated channel-specific bound outperforming the general bound after accounting for evaluation time.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on a drift assumption and calibration age limits; if noise drifts too much or those limits are violated, harmful acceptance can still occur.
paper_title: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents
